instantiate.title: InstantiateMsg
instantiate.description:
Parameters used to instantiate the staking contract.

Pause authorities are intentionally NOT part of instantiate; the owner adds them post-instantiation via [`ExecuteMsg::AddPauseAuthorities`], matching the factory / incentives operator-flow pattern.

minimum_stake_amount.description: Minimum ORO amount per Enter or partial Leave; full exits bypass this. Must be > 0.

oro_denom.description: The ORO token denom that users stake.

execute.title: ExecuteMsg
execute.description: Execute messages exposed by the staking contract.

oneOf.description: Deposit ORO via `info.funds` and credit the sender's stake 1:1.
Begin unbonding `amount` ORO from the caller's stake; queues an entry for `recipient` claimable after `unbonding_period`.
Claim all matured unbonding entries for `info.sender`.

Fund a per-denom reward stream that drips over `duration` seconds. Reward denom and amount come from `info.funds`; RPS is derived on-chain as `amount / duration` so the caller cannot pass a misleading rate. Owner only.
Emergency withdrawal of non-ORO, non-reward-stream tokens accidentally sent to the contract. Owner only.

Update mutable configuration fields. Owner only.

Ownership changes are intentionally NOT exposed here — use the two-step `ProposeNewOwner` + `ClaimOwnership` flow so a fat-fingered hand-off can't strand the contract behind an unreachable address.
Pause the contract. Owner or pause-authority.
Unpause the contract. Owner only.
Add pause-authority addresses. Authorities can `Pause` but cannot `Unpause`, so a compromised authority key cannot grief by toggling. Owner only.
Remove addresses from the pause-authority set. Owner only.
Sweep accumulated orphaned rewards (emissions accrued while no users were staked) to `recipient` or the owner. Owner only.
Propose a new owner; must call `ClaimOwnership` within `expires_in`. Owner only.
Remove the pending ownership proposal. Owner only.
Accept a pending ownership proposal. Proposed-owner only.

migrate.title: MigrateMsg
migrate.description: Message used to trigger a contract migration.

config.title: Config
config.description: Main parameters stored on-chain for the staking contract.

minimum_stake_amount.description:
Minimum ORO amount per Enter or partial Leave; full exits bypass this. Must be > 0.

`#[serde(default)]` makes legacy on-chain bytes (pre-field) deserialise as `Uint128::zero()`; the `migrate` handler then rewrites a non-zero default. New instantiations reject zero up front.

oro_denom.description: The ORO token denom users stake.

paused.description:
Whether the contract is paused.

`#[serde(default)]` is load-bearing: legacy bytes serialised before `paused` existed (pre-2.2.0) deserialise as `false`, so `CONFIG.load()` after `migrate` from such a version succeeds without the migrate handler having to rewrite Config. (Audit N-2.)

Addr.description:
A human readable address.

In Cosmos, this is typically bech32 encoded. But for multi-chain smart contracts no assumptions should be made other than being UTF-8 encoded and of reasonable length.

This type represents a validated address. It can be created in the following ways 1. Use `Addr::unchecked(input)` 2. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_validate(input)?` 3. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_humanize(canonical_addr)?` 4. Deserialize from JSON. This must only be done from JSON that was validated before such as a contract's state. `Addr` must not be used in messages sent by the user because this would result in unvalidated instances.

This type is immutable. If you really need to mutate it (Really? Are you sure?), create a mutable copy using `let mut mutable = Addr::to_string()` and operate on that `String` instance.

total_deposit.description: Total ORO principal backing live stakers (excluding unbonding).

total_shares.description: Sum of all stake balances. Equal to `total_deposit` under the 1:1 model; both fields preserve backwards-compatible JSON shape.

total_shares.title: Uint128

UnbondingEntry.description: A single pending unbonding entry for a user.

oro_amount.description: ORO amount to be returned, fixed at Leave time.

receiver.description: Address that will receive the funds when Claim is called.

reward_coins.description: Accrued reward coins to be returned alongside ORO.

unlock_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which ORO can be claimed.
